ledger.claim: An AIRPORT pickup requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of 480 seconds, and the driver's own trace credits him with 255 seconds — a single run of five qualifying fixes from 23:42:21 to 23:46:36 inside the 150 m radius for this zone class. That is a shortfall of 225 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum for the zone class, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, and the $6.00 must be refunded in full. The trace is impaired at policy level under POL-NS-08(b) — 22.8% coverage, a 52 second sample interval against a 10 second expected cadence, and gaps of 175 and 186 seconds inside the trip — and I disclose that impairment; the shortfall survives the discount because this is the longest qualifying run the record contains and the driver's own trip record independently reports a 6.9 minute wait.

Even if the driver were credited with every single second from the first qualifying in-geofence fix to the moment he cancelled, he still cannot reach 480 seconds. POL-NS-01 limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' tap, and 23:42:21 to the cancellation at 23:49:05 is 404 seconds — 76 seconds short. Neither the 186 second gap that ends at the first fix nor the unfixed tail from the last fix at 23:46:36 to the cancellation can close that gap, because the clause's clock starts no earlier than the trace's own first qualifying fix and stops at the driver's own cancellation. Nothing here requires me to interpolate: the bound is drawn from a derived timestamp in EV-GPS-00210 and the cancellation timestamp in EV-TRIP-00210.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (d) fails on its own, independently of how the dwell is measured. Limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. The trip record shows termination at 23:49:05 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW; the required 480 seconds had not elapsed — measured from his own 'arrived' marker at 23:42:10 they ran out at 23:50:10, and measured as the clause directs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 23:42:21 they ran out at 23:50:21. A cancellation 65 to 76 seconds early is not a termination at or after the elapse of the minimum dwell, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 at all.

The driver's statement that he was at T1 arrival Door 6 'for more than eight minutes' is contradicted by his own device and by his own trip record. The trace holds five qualifying fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT radius across a 255 second run, and the trip record itself reports a 6.9 minute wait — under eight minutes even on the platform's own arrival-tap clock, which is not the clock limb (c) uses. The bundle contains no artifact that corroborates his assertion, and it contains his own telemetry against it.

Satisfying the arrival test does not save the fee, and the driver should not be heard to argue otherwise. POL-NS-02 deems the driver to have arrived where at least three consecutive accurate fixes fall within the radius, and it says in terms that where qualifying in-radius fixes exist 'this clause is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01 limb (c)'. Here arrival is verified and the dwell is 255 seconds against a 480 second minimum, so limb (b) is met, limb (c) is not, and the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 still fails.

The rider's account that he was standing at Door 6 the whole time is not rebutted by this trace, because the trace carries no rider track at all: rider_fix_count is 0 and rider_presence reports available false. POL-NS-04 limb (c) makes an absent rider track UNDECIDABLE and neutral — neither satisfied nor failed — and the rider's presence may not be inferred away from it. I disclose that the omission is itself a defect of the trace under POL-NS-08(b); under POL-GEN-02 an impaired artifact may still be argued on its merits, and here the omission leaves rider presence unproven rather than disproven, which is not the driver's point to win.

The chat record does not show this rider silent or uncooperative. The log contains no driver message of any kind and no reply; trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so POL-NS-04 limb (b) is satisfied on the face of the record. The log is impaired under POL-NS-08(c) — it holds 2 messages against a recorded chat_message_count of 4, its msg_ids run 001 then 004, and it is flagged truncated — so two messages are missing from the very window in issue, and limb (a) cannot be affirmatively denied against the rider on a log that is missing its own messages.

The rider was engaged with the app at the pickup point, not absent from it: he read the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 23:42:30, nineteen seconds after it was sent at 23:42:11, and he messaged the driver at 23:49:40, thirty-five seconds after the cancellation at 23:49:05, asking why the trip was cancelled and stating he was at Door 6. That is the conduct of a rider waiting at the kerb for a car he could not see, and it is the only rider-side record the driver's own truncated log leaves standing.

The driver cannot top his 255 seconds up to the 480 second minimum. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, and whose type is KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, covers the pickup road and the waiting period. EV-ADVIS-00210-01 is MISSING with no payload and carries weight 0.0, and the derived computation records run_count 0, so there is not even a second in-geofence interval to add to the first. The absence of an advisory is itself citable, but it exonerates no one, and the shortfall stands unmodified.

No driver compensation is payable on this record. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 states that where the cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The remedy that follows from this trip's own numbers is the return of the contested $6.00 to the rider, not a payment to the driver out of it.

The disputed $6.00 is still PENDING and refund_issued_sgd stands at 0.00, so NO_ACTION would leave the rider carrying the whole contested charge; the rider is the filing party, so only a refund leaves him not carrying it. And if any part of the deciding fact is held to rest on the trace impaired under POL-NS-08(b), then at the very least the fee must be held rather than collected while the case is reviewed — it must not be taken from the rider in the meantime.

Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is met on the face of the platform's own trip record: TRP-00210 carries a driver 'arrived' event stamped 2026-08-01T23:42:10+08:00, and that event is corroborated to the second by the SYSTEM message 'Your driver has arrived' pushed at 23:42:11.

Limb (d) is met: the trip was terminated by the driver at 23:49:05 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - the status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, started_at is null, and no boarding event is recorded anywhere in the trip record.

Limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are met on the driver's own trace: his minimum distance to the pickup pin is 96.01 m against a 150 m arrival radius for the AIRPORT zone class, and the trace carries 5 consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes. POL-NS-02 says in terms that where qualifying in-radius fixes exist the clause is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01 limb (c) - which is exactly where the driver side argues this case.

The 'arrived' marker at 23:42:10 sits inside a 186-second sampling gap running 23:39:15 to 23:42:21, and the very next fix, 11 seconds later, already places the driver inside the 150 m radius. There is no clock-skew defect here: the marker and the nearest fix are 11 seconds apart, far inside the 90-second limb of POL-NS-08(a), so the arrival event and the GPS record are safely matched.

The rider was told the driver had arrived. The system notification was delivered at 23:42:11 and the rider read it at 23:42:30; she then sent nothing for seven minutes, her only message on the log ('why cancel?? i was at door 6') arriving at 23:49:40, thirty-five seconds after the driver had already cancelled. I disclose that EV-CHAT-00210 is impaired under POL-NS-08(c): it holds 2 messages against the 4 that trip_record.chat_message_count records for this trip, so two messages are not before the tribunal.

The driver's GPS trace is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) and any dwell figure taken from it must be disclosed as impaired. Coverage is 22.8 per cent; the sample interval is 52 seconds against an expected 10; the trace holds only 9 fixes in total; it contains gaps of 175 seconds and 186 seconds, both beyond the 120-second threshold; it carries only 5 fixes across the 23:42:10-23:49:05 waiting window, fewer than the 6 that limb (b) requires; and its final fix at 23:46:36 leaves the last 149 seconds before cancellation completely unobserved.

The longest qualifying in-geofence run reads 255 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, but that figure is bounded by the fixes the trace happens to carry rather than by the driver's actual conduct: he is unobserved across the 186-second gap that straddles the arrival marker and unobserved for the final 149 seconds before he cancelled. On this cadence the 255-second reading is a floor, not a measurement, and it cannot affirmatively establish a shortfall below the minimum.

The shortfall the rider needs under POL-NS-06 is carried by one artifact, and that artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b). POL-NS-08 provides that a claim resting on an impaired artifact cannot alone support a ruling against the party it disfavours, and its closing sentence caps the ruling at PARTIAL_REFUND and sends the case to review under POL-NS-09 where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired. A full refund under POL-NS-06 is therefore not available to the rider on this record, and the disputed fee should be held rather than handed back.

POL-NS-04 cannot be run for the rider. Its limb (c) needs a rider_track, and this trace carries none - the rider_presence block is marked unavailable - so rider presence is undecidable and, by the clause's own words, neutral rather than adverse. The clause requires all three limbs to hold before it exonerates anyone, and limb (c) cannot hold, so no refund flows from POL-NS-04 whatever view is taken of the chat.

POL-NS-05 does not fire either. That clause needs a GPS fix matched to the arrival timestamp showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above, and there is no fix at 23:42:10 at all - the marker falls inside the 23:39:15 to 23:42:21 gap, whose longest single interval is 186 seconds. There is no admissible basis on which to call this a false arrival marker, so the waiting clock is not recomputed and the fee is not voided on this route.

This dispute is rider-filed, the SGD 6.00 charge is still PENDING on the ledger and SGD 0.00 has been refunded. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so on this file declining to disturb the charge is a real disposition that preserves the driver's fee, not a nullity.

Nothing in the driver's profile withholds his compensation. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH limbs, and neither is met: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause demands, and 2 divided by 156 completed trips in 30 days is 0.013, well under the 0.08 rate limb. I cite only those two profile fields, as POL-GEN-01 permits for this test.

The money on the ledger is internally clean, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect to discount: the cancellation fee of SGD 6.00 equals the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is the result fee_schedule.resolution_rule prescribes. On the 80 per cent rate the driver's compensation on this charge is SGD 4.80 of the SGD 6.00.

Neither abuse escalation trigger on the parties' histories is met: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, below the 2 that POL-NS-09(c) requires. Nothing in the profiles takes this case out of an ordinary monetary disposition, so the impairment point above, not the parties' records, is the only matter that could send it to review.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): FULL_REFUND, amount_sgd 6.0, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): FULL_REFUND, amount_sgd 6.0, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
